text:
marco: CI started flaking on the ruby sampleapp onboarding job — getting sporadic 401s from /v1/chat in GH Actions but not locally. anyone seen env-related flakes like this?
anya: hmm, do you run the same docker image locally as in CI? sometimes shell echo adds a newline.
marco: CI uses `ruby:3.2` container. workflow step writes the key with: `- run: echo "${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}" > /tmp/key` then `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /tmp/key)`
sam: that write pattern will include a trailing newline. try `echo -n` or pipe through `tr -d "\n"`.
marco: tried `echo -n` in a debug run, still hit one 401, but most runs pass.
anya: could also be a gem parity issue — what version of the sdk is in the image?
marco: Gemfile.lock had `redwood-sdk (0.3.1)` from when the sampleapp was last updated. CI caches bundles.
sam: we shipped an auth header normalization fix in 0.3.3 that trims header bytes before sending. might explain the sporadic success.
marco: rebuilding the image with 0.3.3 and adding `tr -d '\n'` to the workflow fixed it in 5/5 runs. :tada:
ci-bot: note: workflow 1965432050 re-run 3 — all checks green. link: https://github.com/redwood/example/actions/runs/1965432050
anya: can we make the sampleapp resilient by trimming ENV on load? e.g. in `config/initializers/auth.rb` do `ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']&.strip` and add a test that simulates trailing newline in CI.
sam: agree — minimal middleware and a ci test would save users time. also add a note in quickstart about `echo -n` vs `echo`.
marco: opened PR #412 with: 1) Gem bump to 0.3.3, 2) initializer that strips REDWOOD_API_KEY, 3) GH Actions smoke test that writes the key with a trailing newline and asserts request still succeeds.
ci-bot: PR #412 status: checks/pass. merge queued.
anya: nice small DX win. documented the `echo -n` and added a one-liner in README.
sam: thanks — this should cut onboarding emails. :+1:
